hero.title: Junior Frontend Developer Resume Skills: *the fundamentals* that get you hired
hero.lede: With little or no commercial experience, depth in the basics beats a long tool list. These are the skills hiring managers expect from a junior frontend developer — and how to back each one with a project.

quickAnswer.question: What skills should a junior frontend developer put on a resume?
quickAnswer.answer: Lead with the fundamentals you can demonstrate — HTML, CSS and JavaScript — plus a framework you've built something real in (usually React), version control with Git, and responsive design. At the junior level, employers care less about breadth and more about proof: back each skill with a project, a course build, or an open-source contribution.

faq.q: What skills should a junior frontend developer include with no experience?
faq.a: Focus on the fundamentals you can actually demonstrate: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, a framework like React, Git, and responsive design. Back each with a portfolio project, a bootcamp build, or an open-source contribution. At entry level, depth in the basics and evidence you can ship beats a long list of tools you've only tried once.

faq.q: How many skills should a junior frontend resume list?
faq.a: Around 8–12 well-chosen skills. Enough to cover the fundamentals and the specific technologies a job asks for, but curated to what you can discuss in an interview. A junior resume padded with 30 tools reads as inexperience, not range.

faq.q: Do I need to know React to get a junior frontend job?
faq.a: Not always, but a modern framework helps — React is the most in-demand and a frequent ATS keyword. Solid vanilla JavaScript, HTML and CSS come first; a framework you've built a real project in is the strongest next signal. Match the framework to the jobs you're targeting.

faq.q: Should a junior frontend developer list soft skills?
faq.a: Yes, but show them in context rather than as a generic list. "Collaborated with a designer to ship a responsive landing page" proves communication far better than the word "communication" on its own. Pick a couple you can evidence in a project bullet.
